description: "The creation of transformed training examples to improve a model's robustness or generalization."
term: "Data Augmentation"

difficulty: "Beginner"

## Simple explanation

Data augmentation creates modified versions of training examples, such as
cropped or flipped images, so a model encounters more variation during
training.

## Technical explanation

Augmentations are transformations applied to inputs, labels, or both.
They should preserve the target label and reflect plausible variations in
the intended data. Techniques include image transforms, audio perturbations,
text paraphrases, and synthetic samples. Augmentation policies are
task- and domain-dependent.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Augmentation can help reduce overfitting and improve robustness when
training data is limited. An unrealistic transformation can instead teach
the model incorrect invariances or alter label meaning.

## How it works

During training, a pipeline samples transformations and applies them to
examples, sometimes generating a different view each epoch. Evaluation
data should generally remain unaugmented except for consistent
preprocessing required by the model.

## Practical example

For animal-image classification, small random crops and moderate lighting
changes may help a model handle varied photos. A vertical flip might be
inappropriate if it creates unrealistic images.

## Common misconceptions

- Augmentation does not create new independent information equivalent to
  collecting more diverse data.
- Every transformation is not label-preserving for every task.
- Augmenting validation or test data in ways unavailable at deployment can
  distort evaluation.
